subject: Dev process questions: bugfix branches, issues and features

messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Dev process questions: bugfix branches, issues and features
parts:
The Developer Process wiki page says that bug-fix branches should branch from the latest hotfix branch, but there doesn't seem to be any such branch, and I see bug-fix branches that appear to branch from develop. Has the process changed in this respect?

For feature branches, if the feature does not correspond to an existing issue, is it required to create one?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Dev process questions: bugfix branches, issues and features
parts:
On 2/2/14, 6:30 PM, Kevin Van Horn wrote:
> The Developer Process wiki page says that bug-fix branches should branch from
> the latest hotfix branch, but there doesn't seem to be any such branch, and I see
> bug-fix branches that appear to branch from develop. Has the process changed in this respect?

We've been creating issues just because that's what we review
for planning purposes.

I've just taken to naming branches that fix bugs "bugfix/issue-X-description"
to separate their intent. The key part is that the issue is in the name
so we can search for branches based on issues and vice versa.

I'm not sure we're ever going to be using hotfixes given that we keep
develop in good shape and don't want to maintain historical branches.
But then I haven't been the best adherent to the gitflow.

Feel free to cleanup the language in the Wiki.
> For feature branches, if the feature does not correspond to an existing issue, is it required to create one?

Please do --- it's what we use for planning and it's easy
to search for issues on GitHub using a "#" at the beginning
of the search.

- Bob
